name: Paraparetic Variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Modified Asbury and Cornblath Criteria for Guillain-Barré Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive weakness predominantly affecting the lower limbs without significant upper limb involvement
Decreased or absent deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal cell count
Electrophysiological evidence of demyelination or axonal neuropathy predominantly in lower limbs
Exclusion of other causes of paraparesis such as spinal cord lesions or metabolic neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive paraparesis with areflexia/hyporeflexia and supportive electrophysiological findings, excluding alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on clinical presentation combined with supportive CSF and electrophysiological studies; MRI may be used to exclude spinal cord pathology.

searchTerms: high protein ratio in spinal fluid
increased albumin in CSF compared to blood

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal white cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation)
imaging: MRI spine to exclude compressive myelopathy or other spinal cord pathology
other: Nerve conduction studies showing demyelination or axonal neuropathy predominantly in lower limbs

distinguishingFeatures: MRI evidence of spinal cord lesion
Sensory level and upper motor neuron signs

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness with respiratory compromise
Bulbar muscle involvement causing dysphagia or dysarthria
Autonomic instability with severe cardiac arrhythmias or blood pressure fluctuations
references: Asbury AK, Cornblath DR. Assessment of current diagnostic criteria for Guillain-Barré syndrome. Ann Neurol. 1990.
Orphanet: Paraparetic variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome (ORPHA:231445)
Willison HJ, Jacobs BC, van Doorn PA. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2016.
